Capability row 'dom_asserts met only when selector exists' is unisolated: the manifest's named check (test_absent_text_and_dom_asserts_are_evaluated) contains no dom_asserts assertion at all, so a falsifying edit that ignores selector absence SURVIVES
Capability row 'assertion runs still judged (C7)' is unisolated: no test anywhere constructs Outcome.ASSERTION_FAILED for grade(), so a falsifying edit that refuses to judge assertion runs SURVIVES

Capability row 'ERRORED outranks earlier unmet assert' is unisolated: the fake raises on button.broken inside the handler, so the expectation-bearing step and the exception are the SAME step and no earlier-unmet-assert state is ever built; the exception-masking edit SURVIVES

The unit introduced a UTF-8 BOM plus mojibake em-dash (UTF-8 em-dash bytes re-encoded as latin-1) in tests/test_execute.py's module docstring, and docs/DECISIONS.md gained 4 more mojibake lines in D-032 (pattern pre-existing: 6 lines before -> 10 after; the append script's encoding flaw predates this unit)

assert_expected's docstring promises 'raises nothing' but its url evidence probe is not exception-suppressed: a page.url error during evidence recording propagates and surfaces as ERRORED instead of a recorded unmet assert

Two gate files cite D-056 as the entry authorizing Pathlynks allow_writes. D-056 DOES NOT EXIST. The highest decision id on disk is D-055, across docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/archive/ together. So an authorization that every downstream reader treated as settled was never written, and the question it was supposed to close (write tier / production typing) came back to the human at least three separate times -- which is precisely the cost the append-only log exists to prevent. Nothing forged it; the entry was simply announced in prose and never appended, and no validator anywhere checks that a cited D-NNN resolves.
